claims.text: Sub-5 nm AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles synthesized by pulsed laser deposition on silicon nitride have an FCC structure and initially elliptical shapes.
In sub-5 nm AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles, high surface-to-volume ratios and surface-energy gradients override bulk-like sluggish diffusion.
Minimization of total surface free energy creates a curvature-dependent chemical-potential gradient described by mu = mu0 + Omega gamma kappa.
The curvature-induced chemical-potential gradient drives rapid surface diffusion.
Au and Cu are the low-surface-energy components of AuCoCuNiPt and therefore segregate to the nanoparticle surface.
The tips of elliptical nanoparticles are local chemical-potential maxima because of their high curvature.
Surface diffusion has a lower activation energy than bulk diffusion and is less hindered by HEA lattice distortion.
For particles below 10 nm, the surface-energy contribution to Gibbs free energy dominates the configurational-entropy contribution.
Surface segregation enriches Au and Cu sufficiently to cause their evaporation and nanoparticle shrinkage.
The Gibbs-Thomson effect lowers the effective activation energy for surface diffusion, allowing mass transport significantly below the bulk melting point.
Surface-driven mass transport becomes dominant above a critical temperature of approximately 450 K for sub-5 nm particles.
Above the critical temperature, elliptical particles become spherical within 100 seconds.
Au and Cu surface segregation will be detectable by EDS before significant particle mass loss.
Heating above the critical temperature causes progressive particle mass loss and a narrowing of the size distribution through Ostwald ripening.
The coalescence rate is inversely proportional to the cube of the initial particle radius.
The proposed surface-energy mechanism dominates for radii below 10 nm but does not apply above 50 nm, where bulk sluggish diffusion stabilizes the structure.
Icosahedral particles evolve faster during heating than truncated-octahedral particles because the former have higher surface energy.
Bulk HEA sluggish diffusion can produce high-temperature structural stability.
The prevailing sluggish-diffusion model predicts stabilization against coalescence and segregation to temperatures above 800 K.
Pt evaporation is negligible relative to Au and Cu evaporation.

contradictions.description: The reported observation is a widening size distribution, whereas the hypothesis predicts narrowing. Calling narrowing an Ostwald-ripening outcome is also internally problematic because conventional ripening removes small particles while broadening or coarsening the distribution.
